**Follow-up evidence — the flaky verdict held, and there are now three passes against one failure.**

PR #6847 was re-queued once per the triage checklist and **merged**. Two further data points landed alongside it, both on the same full-suite queue path that ejected it:

| PR | full-suite queue build | `cloud-login-json-ndjson.e2e.test.ts` |
|---|---|---|
| #6846 | merged (`73b723445`) | passed |
| #6852 | merged | passed |
| #6847 | **ejected**, then merged on the single re-queue | failed once at `:333`, passed on re-run |

Three passes and one failure of the same test, within roughly an hour, across four PRs none of which touch `packages/cli`. That closes the remaining alternative — the test is **not** broken on `main`; it is intermittently red under merge-queue load.

This does not lower the priority. It raises the confidence that the diagnosis in the filing is right, and it puts a number on the cost: one ejection in four PRs, each ejection re-building every PR behind it in the queue. The suggested direction stands — make the ordering assertion causal (await the NDJSON line as an event, then drive authorization) rather than temporal, keeping the #6531 ordering guarantee asserted rather than weakening it.

No further action from this seat; recording the observations so the CLI seat inherits the sample rather than re-collecting it.
